items.prompt: Choose the joining word. 'I like apples ___ pears.'
hints: You like both fruits.
We need a word that adds more.
Which word joins two things you like?
items.explanation: And adds more: I like apples and pears.

options.why: But shows something different. Here we add more.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word. 'I was hungry, ___ I ate a banana.'
hints: Being hungry made something happen.
The second part is the result.
Which word means: and that is why?
items.explanation: So tells us what happened because of the first part: I was hungry, so I ate a banana.

options.why: But shows a surprise or a change.
Because gives a reason. Here the reason comes first.

items.prompt: Choose the best joining word. 'I wanted to play outside, ___ it was raining.'
hints: The two ideas do not go well together.
Wanting to play outside and rain make a problem.
Which word shows a change or a problem?
items.explanation: But joins two ideas that clash: I wanted to play outside, but it was raining.

options.why: So would mean the rain happened because you wanted to play.
Because would mean the rain was the reason you wanted to play.
And adds more, but these two ideas clash.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word. 'We took umbrellas ___ it was raining.'
hints: Why did we take umbrellas?
The second part gives a reason.
Which word answers the question why?
items.explanation: Because gives a reason: We took umbrellas because it was raining.

options.why: So would mean the rain came because of the umbrellas.

items.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.
hints: Read each start, then try each ending.
Check that the joining word makes sense.
Start with: I put on my coat. Why?
items.explanation: Because gives a reason, so gives a result, but shows a difference and and adds more.
pairs: so we went to the beach.

items.prompt: Write so or because. 'The shop was closed, ___ we went home.'
hints: Did we go home because of the closed shop?
The second part is what happened next.
Which word shows a result?
items.explanation: So shows a result: The shop was closed, so we went home.

items.prompt: Choose 2 sentences that use because correctly.
hints: Two sentences are right.
Because must give a real reason.
Ask why for each one. Does the answer make sense?
items.explanation: Being happy is a reason to smile, and water is a reason a plant grows.

options.text: I am smiling because I am happy.
I am happy because I am sad.
options.why: Being sad is not a reason to be happy.

options.text: The plant grew because we watered it.
It is sunny because I have a hat.
options.why: Your hat does not make it sunny.

items.prompt: Which word joins these? 'Rina likes to sing. She does not like to dance.'
hints: Rina likes one thing and not the other.
The ideas are different.
Which word shows a difference?
items.explanation: But joins two different ideas: Rina likes to sing, but she does not like to dance.

options.why: And adds more, but these ideas are different.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: Start with the word that has a capital letter.
End with the word that has a full stop.
The joining word goes in the middle, before the reason.
items.explanation: We stayed inside because it was raining. Because joins the reason to what happened.

items.prompt: Which ending makes sense? 'I was tired, so ...'
hints: So tells what happened next.
What do you do when you are tired?
Find the ending that is a result of being tired.
items.explanation: So shows a result. Being tired can make you go to bed early.

options.why: Running a race is not a result of being tired.
This does not follow from being tired.
Tired means you do not have lots of energy.

items.prompt: Which ending makes sense? 'Ben fell over because ...'
hints: Because gives the reason.
The reason happens before the fall.
What could make someone fall?
items.explanation: Because gives the reason. Tripping on a stone made Ben fall.

options.why: Getting a plaster happened after he fell.
Going home happened after he fell.

items.prompt: Choose the best joining word. 'The cake smelled good, ___ it tasted bad.'
hints: Smelled good and tasted bad are different.
The second part is a surprise.
Which word shows a surprise or a change?
items.explanation: But joins two ideas that do not match: smelled good, but tasted bad.

options.why: And adds more. These ideas clash.

items.prompt: Sort the endings. Do they go after because or after so?
hints: Because gives a reason. So gives a result.
Did it happen before the road got wet, or after?
Start with: it rained all night. Did that make the road wet?
items.explanation: Rain and a broken pipe are reasons, so they go after because. Driving slowly and wearing boots are results, so they go after so.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word. 'Pak Ahmad was late ___ his car would not start.'
hints: Why was Pak Ahmad late?
The second part is a reason.
Which word answers why?
items.explanation: Because gives the reason: he was late because his car would not start.

options.why: So would mean the car broke because he was late.
And adds more. Here we need a reason.

items.prompt: Write so or because. 'The dog was dirty, ___ we gave it a bath.'
hints: Which happened first: dirty or bath?
The bath is what we did next.
Which word shows a result?
items.explanation: So shows a result: The dog was dirty, so we gave it a bath.

items.prompt: Which sentence does NOT make sense?
hints: Three sentences make sense.
Check that because gives a real reason.
Does a jumper make you cold?
items.explanation: A jumper does not make you cold, so that sentence does not make sense.

options.text: I was cold, so I put on a jumper.
I put on a jumper because I was cold.
I was cold because I put on a jumper.
I was cold, but I did not have a jumper.

items.prompt: Choose the two joining words. 'I wanted a snack, ___ the tin was empty, ___ I ate an apple.'
hints: Do the gaps one at a time.
The empty tin is a problem.
Eating an apple is what happened next.
items.explanation: But shows the problem, and so shows what happened next.

options.why: So and but are in the wrong places.
Because does not fit the first gap.
Because does not fit the second gap.

items.prompt: Which word is a joining word?
hints: A joining word links two words or ideas.
It can join: cats ___ dogs.
Which word could go in the gap?
items.explanation: And is a joining word. It links words and ideas together.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The sentence has two ideas joined by a joining word.
There is a comma before the joining word.
The joining word shows the first idea is the reason for the second.
items.explanation: I was tired, so I went to bed. The joining word so shows what happened because of the first idea.
items.answer: I was tired, so I went to bed.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The sentence has a reason in it.
The word because comes in the middle.
Why did they stay inside? Because of the weather.
items.explanation: We stayed inside because it was raining. Because joins the action to its reason.
items.answer: We stayed inside because it was raining.

items.prompt: I wanted to play outside, ___ it was raining.
hints: Read both parts of the sentence.
The two parts do not agree with each other.
Which joining word shows a surprise or a problem?
items.explanation: But shows that the second part is different from what you wanted. I wanted to play, but it was raining.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word. I have a cat ___ a dog.
hints: We want to add one more thing.
The joining word adds.
It has three letters.
items.explanation: And joins the cat and the dog.

items.prompt: It was raining, ___ we took umbrellas.
hints: The rain is the reason.
Taking umbrellas is the result.
Use the word for a result.
items.explanation: So shows the result of the rain.

options.why: Because would give the reason the wrong way round.

items.prompt: I like apples, ___ I do not like pears.
hints: The two parts are different.
One is like, one is do not like.
Use the word that shows a difference.
items.explanation: But shows two different ideas.

items.prompt: Tia stayed home ___ she was ill.
hints: The second part tells why.
Why did Tia stay home?
Use the word that gives a reason.
items.explanation: Because gives the reason Tia stayed home.

options.why: So would make the sentence not make sense.

items.prompt: We can walk ___ take the bus.
hints: There are two choices.
You can pick one.
Use the word for a choice.
items.explanation: Or gives a choice between two things.

items.prompt: Write the joining word. I wanted to play, ___ it was raining.
hints: The two parts do not go together.
One is a wish, one stops it.
It is a word with three letters.
items.explanation: But shows the rain stopped the play.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The sentence starts with a capital.
Hungry comes before the joining word.
It ends with a full stop.
items.explanation: I was hungry so I ate rice.
items.answer: I was hungry so I ate rice.

items.prompt: Match each joining word to its job.
hints: Think about what each word does.
Because answers the question why.
And adds one more thing.
items.explanation: Each joining word has its own job.

items.prompt: Which sentence is right?
hints: Being cold is the reason.
Putting on a jumper is the result.
Choose the word for a result.
items.explanation: So shows the result: I put on a jumper.

options.text: I was cold, because I put on a jumper.
options.why: Because gives the reason, but the jumper is the result.

options.text: I was cold, but I put on a jumper.
options.why: But shows a difference, which does not fit here.

options.text: I was cold, so I put on a jumper.
I was cold, or I put on a jumper.

items.prompt: Choose all the joining words.
hints: Joining words connect two ideas.
Two of them are joining words.
Because and one more.
items.explanation: Because and but join ideas.

items.prompt: She is small ___ she is very strong.
hints: Small and strong are different ideas.
One would not expect it.
Use the word that shows the difference.
items.explanation: But shows a surprise: small but strong.
